Important boundaries for this development build.
SharedHouse separates identity verification from household configuration so each server-confirmed step stays clear.
Create an account with an email you can verify and a unique, long password.
Complete email verification before household content becomes available.
Create or edit a household only when the service confirms the change.
If a request fails, review the message and support reference. Do not assume a household change was saved.
The calendar is a household view. It should show actual connected events, not generated examples.
Switch between week, month, quarter and year to change the planning horizon.
Choose a day to open its options and agenda.
Review event details before editing or deleting shared information.
An empty day means no event was returned for that day. It is not a sync-success claim.
Money and expenses
Understand exact splits, payment declarations, suppliers and audited corrections.
Money is a shared ledger, not a bank account. It explains who is included, how each amount was split and what members declared.
Open an expense to check its supplier, amount, due date, notes, exact allocation and payment history.
Record payment creates a declaration with method, time and optional reference; it does not transfer money.
Owners and admins approve proposals. Another eligible member can confirm or dispute a declaration.
Editing an unsettled expense creates a linked revision and moves the original to Reversed.
Removing an expense means reversing it with a reason. Correct active payment declarations first.
Amounts use the household currency and exact minor units. Reload after a version conflict.
Tasks, chores and requests
Learn assignments, recurring chores, completion and help, swap or postpone requests.
Tasks combine a clear assignee and due time with an append-oriented completion and request history.
Use My tasks for your work, Active for the household board and Requests for pending decisions.
Recurring chores run weekly, fortnightly or monthly, with an optional final date, and appear in Calendar.
The server checks membership, role, ownership and current version for every task action.
Ask for help, a swap or postponement with a respectful reason; nothing changes until authorised.
Report a problem when work cannot be completed safely or as described.
A rejected or failed command leaves the confirmed task unchanged.
Household creator and admin guide
Roles, invitations, household configuration, finance controls and automation explained.
Household administration controls shared configuration. It is separate from personal Settings and platform administration.
Set name, country, timezone, currency, week start and billing cycle carefully.
Use People & Access to manage roles and membership through each member’s three-dot menu.
Create invitations with the minimum necessary role; expired or revoked invitations cannot be reused.
Configure people and couples, recurring bills and chore schedules with cadence and optional end dates.
Review consequences before reversals, member removal or ownership transfer.
Existing ledger, chore, membership and payment history remains available after configuration changes.
Household live chat
Understand live status, sending, retries, privacy and notifications.
Chat is scoped to the selected household and streams new messages while open.
Check Live, Connecting or Offline before assuming a message reached other members.
A failed send shows an error and can be retried safely.
Switching households also switches chat scope; other households cannot read it.
Message alerts depend on Android permission and your notification preferences.
Never share passwords, verification codes, bank credentials or unnecessary sensitive data.
Messages are append-only. Live appears only after the service stream is connected.
SharedHouse uses ordinary Android channels. You decide whether the app may notify and which categories remain enabled.
Read the explanation, then request Android permission only if alerts would help.

Automatic reminders use Android background work and never request exact-alarm access. Task notifications can start or complete eligible work directly.

This build distinguishes service-backed, device-only and unavailable capabilities.
Authentication and household configuration use the authoritative service when connected.
Tutorial, appearance and notification preferences are stored on this device.
Money, task and request activity remain unavailable until their APIs are connected.
Unavailable content is never filled with sample balances, chores, members or sync claims.
Use the smallest amount of information needed to coordinate a household.
Appearance, tutorial and alert choices are device preferences.
Identity and household records are service-backed and role-controlled.
Notification previews use private lock-screen visibility by default.
A complete production Privacy Notice and account-data controls must be connected before release. This screen is a product summary, not that notice.
Account security depends on both the app and careful household use.
Use a unique password of at least 15 characters and never share verification codes.
Treat unexpected session or account alerts as important, but not as emergency messages.
Keep support references when reporting a failed service request; never include your password.
The connected session-storage policy must be reviewed before production. Device-management endpoints are not available in this build.
SharedHouse is household coordination software and does not claim to move money or provide emergency services.
Financial views record household information; they are not a bank account or payment rail.
Notifications are ordinary app messages and must never imitate public emergency alerts.
Production Terms, Privacy Notice and regional notices require approved, versioned content.
This is development guidance, not legal advice or a substitute for approved production terms.
